# Composite — C#

*Generated by Claude Opus 5 (claude-opus-5) — Created on 2026-08-04*

For further enquiry please contact Akin Kaldiroglu at akin@kaldiroglu.dev

A C# port of every Composite example in the companion Java repository
(`DesignPatternsWithJava`, package `dev.kaldiroglu.dp.structural.composite`). Same
structures, same figures, same console output.

## What is here

| Namespace | Example |
|-----------|---------|
| `Gof.Graphics` | GoF's Motivation (p. 163) — a graphics editor: `Graphic`, `Line`, `Rectangle`, `Text`, `Picture` |
| `Gof.Equipment` | GoF's Sample Code (pp. 170–173) — cabinets, chassis, buses and cards, with price and power roll-ups |
| `Bom.Domain` | `Money` and `Catalog` — the figures both bill-of-materials designs are built from |
| `Bom.Problem` | The same bill of materials **without** the pattern: no shared type, two child collections, the recursion copied into every client |
| `Bom.Solution` | The same problem **with** the pattern: `BomComponent`, `Part`, `Service`, `Assembly`, and `BomLine` carrying the quantity |
| `Drawing` | Shapes on a canvas — the **safe** variant, child management on `ICompositeGraphic` |
| `FileSystem` | Files, directories and links — roll-ups, a cached total, upward invalidation, and a depth-first iterator |
| `Hw.OrgChart` | Homework 1 — the roll-up, and what a shared report costs it |
| `Hw.SurveyForm` | Homework 2 — the **transparent** variant, where `Add` on a leaf compiles and throws |
| `Hw.Expression` | Homework 3 — an expression tree, where the tree *is* the arithmetic |

## The one deliberate difference from Java

The Java package `composite.graphic` becomes the C# namespace **`Drawing`**. In Java a
lowercase package `graphic` and a type `Graphic` coexist; in C# a namespace that shares a
type's name shadows it, and `Composite.Graphic` made the GoF `Graphic` type unreachable from
anywhere under `Composite`. Everything else keeps the Java names.

Two spellings follow C# convention rather than Java's: interfaces are `IStorage`,
`IGraphic`, `IEmployee`, `IFormElement`, `IExpression`, and Java getters become properties
where they are plain reads.

## Both sides of GoF's issue 4, on purpose

Where child management lives is the decision students most often get wrong, so the examples
take both sides and say which:

| Example | `Add`/`Remove` declared on | Side |
|---------|---------------------------|------|
| `Gof.Graphics`, `Gof.Equipment` | the Component — as the book has it | transparent |
| `Bom.Solution` | `Assembly`, the Composite | safe |
| `Drawing` | `ICompositeGraphic` | safe |
| `FileSystem` | `IStorageContainer` | safe |
| `Hw.SurveyForm` | the Component — `IFormElement` | transparent |
| `Hw.OrgChart` | `Manager` only | safe |

## Run it with

```bash
# every example, in the order the course covers them
dotnet run --project src/Composite.Demo

# the tests
dotnet test
```

> **SDK note.** The repository root pins .NET 10 in `global.json` with
> `rollForward: latestMajor`, which does not roll *back*. On a machine whose newest SDK is 9,
> add a `global.json` beside this README pinning the installed version, or install .NET 10.
